title: Time and Physical Geometry
kind: primary journal article; JSTOR scan via public mirror
version: The Journal of Philosophy 64(8), 27 April 1967, 240-247; JSTOR stable URL 2024493
locator: Principles (1) and assumptions i-iii pp. 240-241; (2) and transitivity argument p. 243; Aristotle and truth-value-gap argument with footnote 1 pp. 243-245; 'Morals and Conclusions' and transitive-closure conclusion p. 246
assumptions: (1) All (and only) things that exist now are real
i I-now am real; ii another observer in relative motion is real
III There Are No Privileged Observers, stated tenselessly with R physical, coordinate-independent, tenselessly definable, non-accidental
Special relativity; Lorentz invariance of laws; enough observers incl. all physical systems
conclusion: Future and past events are real (transitive closure of 'simultaneous in the coordinate system of x'); truth-value gaps for future contingents would define an Absolute Simultaneity, contradicting relativity
proof_status: Published argument; authors' claim read in full; its gap (R need not be slice-like) is documented in bridges-stein-1991
relevance: Strongest primary defense of Bridge A (physical supervenience of concrete existence): the ontological conclusion is derived from explicitly physical premises
limits: OCR-derived text with punctuation artifacts; page images not inspected line-by-line; the famous objection (R = causal past satisfies III without the conclusion) is in Stein, not in this text

title: On Relativity Theory and Openness of the Future
kind: primary journal article; project print audit of user-supplied JSTOR scan (SHA-256 fef0224102cca5037a9da1878f541ee074e64412fe71e52504b94ebc915153f7, local, not committed)
locator: Theorem p. 149 plus prose conditions: non-universality (iv) and causal-past inclusion (timelike or null); ontological-probabilism claim p. 164 as quoted in Pooley 2013 preprint section X
assumptions: R reflexive, transitive, invariant under time-orientation-preserving automorphisms
conclusion: R coincides with the past-pointing (causal) relation; becoming in SR is standpoint-local and definable from Minkowski structure
proof_status: Printed theorem verified against page images by project audit; audit also gives the strict-chronological countermodel showing the displayed hypotheses alone are insufficient
relevance: Charitable rival rejection of Bridge A and primary defense of the definability half of Bridge C: no slice-like invariant reality relation; becoming without added structure
limits: Only pp. 148-150 of the scan were OCRed and checked by the project audit; the p. 164 ontological-probabilism quote is taken via Pooley 2013 (secondary)

title: What becomes of a causal set
kind: primary article preprint; partial read
version: arXiv:1502.00018v1 (30 January 2015), 22 pages; journal: British Journal for the Philosophy of Science (2016), DOI 10.1093/bjps/axv040; journal version not collated
locator: v1 pp. 1-13 read: intro, section 2 basics, section 3 (dilemma p. 5; Stein theorem discussion; counterexample causet Figure 1 and non-Hegelian pairs; Lorentz-violation argument pp. 8-9), section 4 through the Smart-objection discussion p. 13
assumptions: Causal set kinematics; CSG dynamics for the growth discussion
conclusion: Any present-identification either answers the A-theorist's explanatory request or is compatible with the structure, but not both (p. 5); the Stein analogue fails in CST kinematics but the escape fails generically; 'rather than escape the dilemma, it seems CST embraces it and even makes it rigorous' (p. 9)
proof_status: Authors' philosophical claims; the Figure-1 counterexample is elementary and inspectable in their text; no formal novelty claim made here
relevance: Primary source for the rigorous dilemma version of Bridge C and for the category-relativity countermodel (Stein analogue is structure-dependent)
limits: Sections 4.5 onward and section 5 (their novel global becoming) not read this session; the project's bridge-defense note cites v1 sections 4-5 separately; journal pagination not collated

title: Relativity, the Open Future, and the Passage of Time
kind: primary article author preprint (PhilSci-Archive 9936); substantial partial read; also located: talk copy at oliverpooley.org/files/AS-June2013.pdf
version: Preprint of paper published in Proceedings of the Aristotelian Society 113(3) (2013); published version not collated
locator: Section II B-theory characterization ('exhaustive catalogue... complete account of temporal reality'); sections III-V classical views incl. Skow 2009 quotes pp. 666-675; section VI open-future/branching; section VII 'Against a Preferred Now' (neo-Lorentzian dilemma and superadded-foliation cost); sections VIII-X Earman's hypersurface/worldline becoming, Skow's superspacetime, BST and Stein's ontological probabilism
assumptions: Standard relativistic spacetime structure; local physics of SR
conclusion: Three routes for passage plus relativity (deflation, preferred Nows, non-standard no-global-Now); the preferred-Now route faces a dilemma with stated costs; properly relativistic becoming requires non-standard A-theoretic resources
proof_status: Published author's arguments (preprint); quoted sources (Skow, Earman, Dieks, Maudlin, McCall, Belnap) verified only as quoted here
relevance: Primary statement of the cost accounting for added-structure routes (Bridge C) and of the B-theoretic completeness claim (Bridge B defense)
limits: Final section(s) of the preprint beyond section X not read; published pagination not collated; fn. 6 characterization of Maudlin is Pooley's, not Maudlin's own text

title: Spacetime as a causal set: Universe as a growing block?
kind: primary journal article; open-access PDF
locator: Abstract; section 1 intro incl. Earman 2008, 159 quote p. 37; section 3 CSG definitions and discrete general covariance pp. 39-42; section 4 central argument: covariant sigma-algebra, stems, rogues (Brightwell et al. Proposition 1), condition [N], Choices 1-2 pp. 46-51; conclusion (completion-parasitism) printed pp. 51-52
assumptions: CSG dynamics of Rideout-Sorkin; discrete general covariance; truth-supervenience presuppositions behind [N]
conclusion: The CSP with CSG dynamics does not support growing-block Becoming: the dynamics is defined only on completed causal sets (parasitic on the block), and covariance strips the theory of physically significant propositions whose truth supervenes on the already-become part
proof_status: Published argument relying on Brightwell et al. 2003 Proposition 1 (rogues have measure zero), not independently re-derived here
relevance: Primary completion-parasitism argument against Bridge B's ontological completeness reading; also documents that CSG 'local becoming' is not novel against SR discussions (his section 4 Choice 2)
limits: Finite-document read; his bracketing of metaphysical worries about local becoming is explicit; Stein 1968 and Dieks 2006 locators are his citations, not independently read
